hints: Remember a redox reaction must show a change in oxidation number, with one element oxidised and another reduced.
Check sulfur in option C first, it goes from +4 in $\text{SO}_2$ to +6 in $\text{SO}_3$, so that one is definitely redox.
Now track S, O and H in $\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and see if any oxidation number actually changes.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for redox**

A reaction is redox only if oxidation numbers change. Oxidation is an increase in oxidation number, reduction is a decrease.

Rule to use:
$$\text{redox if oxidation number changes, non-redox if all stay the same}$$

**Spot the obvious redox reactions**

In A, $\text{Mg}$ goes $0 \rightarrow +2$ (oxidised) and H goes $+1 \rightarrow 0$ in $\text{H}_2$ (reduced). In C, S goes $+4 \rightarrow +6$ (oxidised) and N goes $+4 \rightarrow +2$ (reduced).

Key changes:
$$\text{A: Mg(0 to +2), H(+1 to 0)}$$ $$\text{C: S(+4 to +6), N(+4 to +2)}$$

**Check the remaining two**

In B, thermal decomposition of a nitrate, N goes $+5 \rightarrow +4$ and O goes $-2 \rightarrow 0$, so it is also redox. In D, S stays at $+6$, O stays at $-2$, and H stays at $+1$ on both sides.

For D:
$$\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4: \text{no change in any oxidation number}$$

**Conclude**

Only the reaction with no change in oxidation number is not redox. That is the formation of sulfuric acid from sulfur trioxide and water.

options.A: This is redox. Mg is oxidised from 0 in $\text{Mg}$ to +2 in $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$, while H is reduced from +1 in $\text{HNO}_3$ to 0 in $\text{H}_2$. It is a typical metal plus acid displacement.
options.B: This is redox. Although Mg stays +2, N is reduced from +5 in $\text{NO}_3^-$ to +4 in $\text{NO}_2$, and O from the nitrate is oxidised from -2 to 0 in $\text{O}_2$. All Group 2 nitrate decompositions are redox for this reason.
options.C: This is redox. S is oxidised from +4 in $\text{SO}_2$ to +6 in $\text{SO}_3$, while N is reduced from +4 in $\text{NO}_2$ to +2 in $\text{NO}$. This is a key step in the Contact process chemistry.
options.D: This is not redox. In $\text{SO}_3$, S is +6 and O is -2. In $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, H is +1 and O is -2. In $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, H is +1, S is +6 and O is -2. No oxidation numbers change, so it is simply an acid-base hydration reaction.
